The tail device M5 is the most likely corrupted element. It is the only transistor not in saturation: its Vds of 0.257 V is below its Vdsat of 0.546 V. Its W/L mirror ratio against M6 (4.12) should supply about 41 µA, but it carries only 29.4 µA, which is the signature of a tail that has been pushed into triode. The most probable fault is a wrong W/L on M5, which sets the tail mirror ratio. The f0 sensitivities don't single out one element cleanly. R3's +1.19e8% figure looks like a numerical artifact of an MHz-scale peak appearing, so I rank it second, and M6 (the bias diode that sets the mirror reference) third.

Restore M5 to a W/L that keeps it saturated (lower mirror ratio / larger headroom), which also restores the diff-pair bias and the f0 shift."}
